title: RFI USMMA Campus Modernization Program SATOC Seawall Project
agency: DEPT OF DEFENSE > DEPT OF THE ARMY > USACE > NAD > W2SD ENDIST NEW YORK
description:
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY  

 This announcement is issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), New York District, is seeking information regarding the interest, capability, and qualifications of firms that may be capable of performing the requirement described below.  

 This RFI is for planning and informational purposes only. It does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposals (RFP), Invitation for Bids (IFB), or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  

 The Government will not pay for, reimburse, or otherwise compensate respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The Government does not intend to rank submissions or provide individual responses to interested firms. Information submitted and clearly marked as “Proprietary” will be handled accordingly. 

 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New York District is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity, Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) to determine interest, capabilities, and qualifications to for Design-Build contractors. The NAICS codes for this procurement is 237990, Size Standard is $45 Million.  The Request for Proposals is planned to be issued in the Spring of 2027 with construction to begin early in 2028. The estimated SATOC capacity is $70,000,000 with the anticipated Task Order magnitude between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000.  Work under this contract is expected to begin in winter of 2028. 

 The SATOC will be for contractor to replace/restore 2,800-foot seawall at the United States Merchant Marine Academy, Kings Point, NY.  The project will be constructed within the access-controlled installation along the waterfront of the United States Merchant Marine Academy.  Adjacent facilities will remain occupied during construction with minimal disruption to operations requiring precise construction planning. Work for this project is described below: 

 1. Project Purpose and Program Context 
USACE and USMMA have undertaken an agreement to modernize the campus in its entirety providing upgraded Barracks, Academic Buildings, Training Buildings, Athletic Facilities and Waterfront Spaces. The Seawall will serve to protect critical land side facilities essential to the education and training of Midshipmen from storm, wave action, and tidal erosion. 

 ________________________________________ 
2. Existing Conditions 
The existing seawall along the United States Merchant Marine Academy (USMMA) campus shoreline extends approximately 2,800 linear feet and is aligned generally north–south along the western waterfront. The seawall exhibits significant variability in height, construction type and functional purpose along with its length. 

 At the northern end (north of Hague Basin), the shoreline protection system transitions through several construction types in sequence: beginning with a timber (wooden) bulkhead, followed by a stone and mortar wall, then reverting to a timber bulkhead and transitioning to a steel sheet pile bulkhead with a concrete cap. (See Attachment - USMMA Seawall Site Map) 

 Within the Hague Basin, the shoreline structures consist primarily of steel sheet pile bulkheads and stone façade walls. Presume the stone façade walls incorporate a concrete core based on visual assessment.  South of Hague Basin, the shoreline is predominantly stabilized by a concrete seawall with riprap protection, which further transitions to cast-in-place (poured) concrete only toward the southern extent.  The southernmost seawall segment, segment 9, includes stabilizing the adjacent slope to address its instability, mitigate further erosion, and support a future 12 ft. wide roadway/walkway to connect existing roads on campus. 
________________________________________ 
3. Design and Construction Scope 
This project will rehabilitate/restore 2,800-feet of seawall at the United States Merchant Marine Academy.   The scope includes progressing the government provided 35% design consisting of nine segments to 100% Design, completing all required permitting documents, reconstructing the seawall, and restoring the waterfront. 

 The contractor will review, validate, and advance the government-furnished 35% Design RFP package to 65% and 100% Issued for Construction (IFC) submittals across civil, structural, coastal, and geotechnical disciplines.  Following design finalization for a segment construction will commence to remove and/or restore the degraded segment of seawall. 

 The contractor will be required to complete the work in accordance with all required permits, certifications and licenses required by Federal, State, and local law for the execution of this work. 

 ________________________________________ 
4. Design Standards and Performance Requirements 
All work will meet the USMMA Campus Design Guide and Engineering Design Standards which contain DOT standards including the International Building Code (IBC), GSA standards, and DoD Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC). 

 ________________________________________ 
5. Acquisition Strategy and Contracting Approach 
The Government intends to establish a Design-Build (D-B) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a total contract capacity of $70,000,000 over an anticipated five-year ordering period.
